description: Full canonical KB records and column metadata; FTS shadow/duplicate indexes excluded

table_schemas.kb_decisions:
CREATE TABLE kb_decisions (
  decision_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  topic TEXT NOT NULL,
  decision TEXT NOT NULL,
  rationale TEXT NOT NULL,
  scope TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (scope IN ('global','project','campaign')),
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('locked','proposed','blocked','retired')),
  owner TEXT NOT NULL,
  source_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES kb_sources(source_id),
  next_review TEXT
)
table_schemas.kb_facts:
CREATE TABLE kb_facts (
  fact_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  domain TEXT NOT NULL,
  subject_no INTEGER,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  statement TEXT NOT NULL,
  scope TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (scope IN ('global','project','campaign','historical')),
  evidence_class TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (evidence_class IN ('canonical','static','deterministic','created_document','safe_use','full_function','historical','blocked','local','staged','fixture')),
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('locked','active','provisional','superseded','blocked')),
  source_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES kb_sources(source_id),
  supersedes_fact_id TEXT REFERENCES kb_facts(fact_id),
  tags TEXT DEFAULT ''
)
table_schemas.kb_metadata:
CREATE TABLE kb_metadata (
  key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  value TEXT NOT NULL
)
table_schemas.kb_milestones:
CREATE TABLE kb_milestones (
  milestone_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  milestone TEXT NOT NULL,
  goal TEXT NOT NULL,
  deliverables TEXT NOT NULL,
  exit_gate TEXT NOT NULL,
  dependencies TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('planned','ready','in_progress','blocked','complete')),
  source_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES kb_sources(source_id)
)
table_schemas.kb_open_items:
CREATE TABLE kb_open_items (
  item_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  item_class TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (item_class IN ('research','implementation','certification','defect','reconciliation','release')),
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  problem TEXT NOT NULL,
  next_action TEXT NOT NULL,
  evidence_needed TEXT NOT NULL,
  priority TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (priority IN ('P0','P1','P2','P3')),
  status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('open','in_progress','blocked','closed')),
  owner TEXT NOT NULL,
  source_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES kb_sources(source_id)
)
table_schemas.kb_relationships:
CREATE TABLE kb_relationships (
  relationship_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  from_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  from_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  relation TEXT NOT NULL,
  to_type TEXT NOT NULL,
  to_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  notes TEXT
)
table_schemas.kb_research_subjects:
CREATE TABLE kb_research_subjects (
  subject_no INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  subject TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL,
  depth TEXT NOT NULL,
  project_delta TEXT NOT NULL,
  community_research TEXT NOT NULL,
  next_step TEXT NOT NULL,
  source_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES kb_sources(source_id)
)
table_schemas.kb_sources:
CREATE TABLE kb_sources (
  source_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
    source_kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source_kind IN ('canonical','project','campaign','conversation','external','research','verification')),
  scope TEXT NOT NULL,
  authority TEXT NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL,
  location TEXT NOT NULL,
  captured_at TEXT,
  version_fingerprint TEXT,
  notes TEXT
)
table_schemas.kb_tools:
CREATE TABLE kb_tools (
  tool_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  project_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  project_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  tool_name TEXT NOT NULL,
  tool_kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (tool_kind IN ('command','harness','verifier','adapter','runtime','query','schema','target','source')),
  invocation TEXT NOT NULL,
  location TEXT NOT NULL,
  capability TEXT NOT NULL,
  authority TEXT NOT NULL,
  evidence_status TEXT NOT NULL,
  source_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES kb_sources(source_id),
  tags TEXT DEFAULT ''
)
table_schemas.kb_trials:
CREATE TABLE kb_trials (
  trial_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  area TEXT NOT NULL,
  symptom TEXT NOT NULL,
  attempted_approach TEXT NOT NULL,
  failure_cause TEXT NOT NULL,
  correction TEXT NOT NULL,
  evidence_status TEXT NOT NULL,
  source_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES kb_sources(source_id)
)

rows.decision: Name the central project DiceBox Campaign Helper and use it for the program plus associated Foundry VTT module.
rows.rationale: Provides one stable project identity while preserving the previous Campaign Assistant research as foundation.

rows.decision: Expose a small semantic public API: describe, supports, execute, query, resolve, health.
rows.rationale: Prevents arbitrary Foundry mutation and gives the module a stable bridge contract.

rows.decision: Compile D&D5e mechanics Activity-first, then Midi composition, then Effects/DAE, Region/Scene, Additional Activity, and macro only as last resort.
rows.rationale: Uses native system semantics and avoids giant procedural macros.

rows.decision: Treat the active GM as authoritative executor for protected player-triggered world mutations.
rows.rationale: Foundry permissions reject direct player updates and active-GM routing prevents duplicate writers.

rows.decision: Freeze Spatial Blueprint before map art or Foundry placeable compilation.
rows.rationale: Avoids geometry drift, misaligned grids, invented doors, and image-first topology errors.

rows.decision: Use SQLite with normalized tables plus FTS5 search for the central KB.
rows.rationale: Keeps provenance, facts, trials, open work, research, and milestones queryable without requiring an external service.

rows.decision: Mark capabilities unavailable or unverified when exact runtime proof is missing; fail closed or use a verified fallback.
rows.rationale: Prevents source/test/chat success from becoming false live certification.

rows.decision: Keep campaign packs separate from global module contracts.
rows.rationale: Prevents Iggwilv/Prime Arachnid content and authored UUIDs from becoming hidden global assumptions.

rows.decision: Create the dicebox-campaign-helper Foundry package and manifest during M2, even while the first runtime is read-only.
rows.rationale: A valid package boundary is required for clean load, compatibility checks, and later updates.

rows.decision: Use modifyBatch only for independent operations; use staged journaled transactions for dependent IDs and cross-document links.
rows.rationale: Matches Foundry v14 batch semantics and preserves recovery information.

rows.decision: Treat the SQLite KB as a compiled read-only index until edit synchronization, migrations, and FTS triggers are implemented.
rows.rationale: Avoids stale or inconsistent search results while retaining a reproducible local build.

rows.decision: Use Campaign Continuity / Campaign Safe Mode as the provisional first-product thesis; keep Player Turn Coach as a later feature or bundle.
rows.rationale: The competitor pass shows action access, reminders, tracking, timing, planning, memory, and AI continuation are already served by adjacent products. A typed, inspectable, selectively mergeable session branch offers a narrower GM-paid outcome and stronger reuse of DiceBox safety/provenance assets.

rows.decision: Treat cross-VTT support as a neutral session-packet boundary, not a universal live-sync promise.
rows.rationale: Player-facing companion features are crowded and platform APIs differ. A portable packet can widen the market without pretending Roll20, Fantasy Grounds, and Foundry share one mutation model.

rows.decision: Use Campaign Continuity as the public product name and Campaign Safe Mode as the internal feature name.
rows.rationale: The public promise is a visible continuity outcomeâ€”continue after disruption, compare the branch, keep or discardâ€”while Safe Mode sounds like invisible infrastructure. The rename remains provisional until message testing.

rows.decision: Use the Canon & Branch Board as the provisional public hero surface, not as a separate campaign wiki.
rows.rationale: The current Foundry premium catalog rewards immediate visual outcomes. A branch-backed timeline and semantic diff can create a glanceable demo while preserving the real value: recovery effort, hidden-state protection, and selective canonization.

rows.decision: Run Campaign Continuity and Campaign Guardian as separate head-to-head offers before combining or selecting one.
rows.rationale: Continuity has a differentiated branch/merge concept but mixed urgency; Guardian has stronger game-night fear but competes with free backup workflows. A direct recent-pain and purchase-choice comparison is the next valid selection step.

rows.decision: Reject Campaign Guardian, generic Campaign Replay, and generic improvisation as standalone first products; retain their useful behaviors as features or alternatives.
rows.rationale: Current Foundry, Forge, Battle Replay, Encounter Forge, RPGM Forge, Escalating Encounters, and Perceived Reality cover the broad promises. Continue testing only the narrower semantic non-combat branch/merge outcome.

rows.decision: Prototype Campaign Continuity as a read-only/preview-first Foundry branch with staged GM-authorized merge; do not claim atomic rollback or universal state coverage.
rows.rationale: Official v14 API primitives support serialization, ephemeral clones, validation, permission checks, and document operations, but cross-document transaction and module-owned-state limits require explicit recovery and unsupported-state boundaries.

rows.decision: Reject Campaign Continuity / Campaign Safe Mode as the first storefront product; retain its branch, provenance, visibility, reset, and recovery mechanics as reusable infrastructure.
rows.rationale: The five-second promise remains weak, the problem is episodic, and current backups, notes, duplicate worlds, dashboards, and continuity tools provide credible alternatives. A polished board does not yet prove a paid outcome.

rows.decision: Open the next candidate as Adventure Capsules: short, ready-to-run, player-visible premium sessions with reusable continuity/reset support.
rows.rationale: A finished evening with visible scenes, reveals, handouts, and choices is more glanceable and repeat-purchasable than invisible campaign safety, but premium adventures and map packs are direct competitors and buyer choice is untested.

rows.decision: Reject generic Adventure Capsules and narrow the candidate to Adaptive Drop-In Capsules for variable attendance and no-canon side sessions.
rows.rationale: Current premium adventures already provide ready-to-run content and visual polish. The only untested wedge with a clearer recurring job is a rapid, bounded side session that preserves the main campaign when attendance changes.

rows.decision: Run the next Foundry test only in a bounded disposable fixture and keep the manifest preflight separate from live readiness.
rows.rationale: The exact target stack is locally available, but no live ready-hook, authority, document, failure-recovery, or read-back evidence exists. Existing campaign worlds must remain untouched.

rows.decision: Keep Campaign Continuity / Safe Mode out of the storefront and test Game Night Rescue as the provisional productized form of Adaptive Drop-In Capsules.
rows.rationale: The new message is visually and emotionally clearer, but its paid unit must be a finished no-canon capsule plus attendance and safe-exit workflow. No implementation or product selection is authorized until recent buyer pain and real purchase choice are observed.

rows.decision: Market the candidate with a trigger-to-payoff demonstration and trust proof.
rows.rationale: A five-second â€œplayer absent â†’ game continuesâ€ sequence, first-minute playable proof, exact compatibility, no-canon boundary, rights disclosure, and reviews are more legible than safety or branch terminology. This is a test plan, not evidence of conversion.

rows.decision: Test Game Night Rescue first with paid/professional GMs and high-variance organizers, not as a broad home-game product.
rows.rationale: Home tables often have low-cost social workarounds, while paid and organized hosts have measurable prep, booking, and retention value. If that payer cohort does not choose the product at a real price, reject the candidate and reopen the search.

rows.decision: Retain DMF as a serious competing candidate, but test it as Custom Item Workshop rather than as a generic AI item creator or raw Midi-QOL script generator.
rows.rationale: The local project has a credible end-to-end automation gap, while plain item generation has direct competition and simple items have cheap alternatives. Product selection requires buyer evidence from ordinary and automation-heavy GMs.

rows.decision: Retain DMF compiler, review, capability, provenance, and verification assets regardless of which storefront candidate wins.
rows.rationale: These assets can support Game Night Rescue or a future cross-VTT recipe compiler, but technical reuse must not be treated as proof that DMF itself is marketable.

rows.decision: Position DMF as the automation completion layer beyond Automaker, not as a faster basic item generator.
rows.rationale: Automaker establishes a strong speed/direct-insertion baseline. DMF should win only when a custom item needs cross-module wiring, dependency explanation, repair, and verification.

rows.decision: Make DMF Foundry-first with a portable neutral recipe/receipt boundary and separate future VTT adapters.
rows.rationale: Foundry Activities, Midi-QOL, DAE, and Item Macro are not shared runtime contracts with Roll20 or Fantasy Grounds. Portability is honest at the intent/evidence layer; live automation needs distinct projections and verification.

rows.decision: Open Foundry Upgrade Guardian as the leading fresh product hypothesis and keep DMF backburnered as an internal compiler asset.
rows.rationale: Upgrade breakage is recurring, broad, visible, and connected to paid modules and active campaigns. Existing backups and compatibility tools create a clear but unproven gap for world-specific disposable rehearsal and smoke-test receipts.

rows.decision: Implement Upgrade Guardian first as a local setup companion with an optional Foundry probe, not as a self-modifying in-world module.
rows.rationale: The active world cannot safely replace its own runtime or rehearse a future stack in place. A closed-world companion workflow preserves the live campaign and supports explicit evidence labels, while avoiding redistribution of Foundry or premium content.

rows.decision: Do not select generic Upgrade Guardian; retain Campaign Runtime Locker as a conditional self-hosted hypothesis.
rows.rationale: Foundry already supplies pre-update compatibility checks, backups, portable builds, and multi-version guidance, while hosting services sell version switching and snapshots. The remaining wedge is per-world known-good runtime locking and one-click local launch, which must beat manual installs and hosting in a real price test.

rows.decision: Reject a generic performance monitor; retain Session Health Autopsy as a conditional new-product hypothesis.
rows.rationale: Current modules already monitor performance, optimize rendering, adjust per-player profiles, and bisect modules. The only plausible wedge found is an eye-catching guided incident workflow that correlates affected clients with scene/assets/module events and produces a reversible action plan. It must earn a real GM price choice before implementation.

rows.decision: Reject a generic mobile companion; keep a low-bandwidth browser relay as a secondary conditional hypothesis.
rows.rationale: Foundry's core gap is real and Roll20's browser investment validates demand, but current Foundry products already cover mobile sheets, touch controls, maps, chat, combat, and invite-based companions. A relay is worth testing only if it reaches weaker devices with less setup and lower resource use than those alternatives.

rows.decision: Advance Thin Client Player Relay as the leading conditional buyer hypothesis, not as a full mobile companion.
rows.rationale: The payer pass found explicit â‚¬15â€“â‚¬25 price anchors and a current â‚¬15 lifetime competitor, while full mobile companion capabilities are already occupied. The next test should target the unverified thin-client wedge: no app installation, low bandwidth, weak-device reach, and a Foundry-authoritative action gateway.

rows.decision: Pass the static technical and licensing screen for a Foundry-first thin client, but do not certify the product yet.
rows.rationale: Official module sockets, public APIs, connected clients, role/document permissions, and licensing guidance support a narrow module-mediated relay. They do not prove external browser authentication, reconnect behavior, weak-device performance, full Activity/Midi-QOL fidelity, or cross-VTT live execution. Reject any design that requires a cloud control plane, direct player document writes, private API guarantees, or bundled protected content; advance only to an exact disposable read-only/typed-request fixture.

rows.decision: Retain Player Flow / Tabletop Ease Mode as an alternate conditional hypothesis; reject generic HUD and generic accessibility as standalone products.
rows.rationale: Community evidence shows recurring player confusion and choice overload, while Foundry Navigator, Accessibility Enhancements, Stylish Action HUD, and party-inventory tools already cover slices of the problem. The only plausible new wedge is a per-player, task-driven cockpit that removes choices and reduces GM interruptions across systems. It must beat existing HUDs and simple onboarding in a direct task and price test before implementation.

rows.decision: Reject Player Flow / Tabletop Ease Mode as a standalone first product; retain its task-graph, guidance, and accessibility components for the Thin Client Player Relay or a bundled content product.
rows.rationale: Foundry already provides player tutorials and a knowledge base, while communities solve the problem with training sessions, mini-campaigns, screen sharing, existing HUDs, or simpler VTTs. A paid Beginner Box shows that onboarding can support a valuable content bundle, but no direct price evidence supports a generic cockpit. Reopen only if a future buyer test produces actual GM payment or pilot commitment.

rows.decision: Reject generic drawing and collaborative whiteboard as a standalone first product; retain geometry/export auditing as a reusable component.
rows.rationale: Recent users report drawing pain, but native Foundry, active drawing/wall modules, Owlbear, Miro, and paid MapForge occupy the obvious product surface. The narrower geometry audit is more creator-facing than the requested wide buyer market.

rows.decision: Advance Monster Field Guide / Creature Codex as the fresh leading conditional product hypothesis.
rows.rationale: The 2024 Study action supplies an ordinary D&D5e hook; ANewFoe proves the category; PF2E Bestiary Tracking shows current selective-reveal value; and a tiered evidence-backed codex has a more visible payoff than Safe Mode or another HUD. Payment and exact runtime evidence remain absent.

rows.decision: Do not implement Monster Field Guide until the qualified-GM, rights, portability, and exact disposable-runtime gates pass.
rows.rationale: The payer is a GM with recurring knowledge-heavy play, while the rights-safe boundary is user-owned actor data and GM-entered notes. A neutral knowledge packet is portable, but live permissions and checks are platform-specific. Reject if the buyer sees bookkeeping, chooses no price, or hidden-state protection fails.

rows.decision: Reject generic trade, treasury, campaign wiki, and campaign-memory products as fresh wide-market candidates.
rows.rationale: Item Piles, focused trade modules, RPGX Loot Crate, Campaign Codex, World & Campaign Builder, Familiar, and external note systems already cover the broad jobs. Preserve transaction receipts, permissions, relationships, and notes as reusable assets.

rows.decision: Keep Monster Field Guide only as a downgraded conditional lead: modern D&D5e evidence-to-knowledge layer, not a generic bestiary.
rows.rationale: ANewFoe covers almost all baseline behavior, PF2E Bestiary Tracking validates the category, and current campaign-memory products reduce the value of a broad codex. The only plausible wedge is evidence/provenance/Study integration with a visible table payoff, subject to real GM payment and pilot evidence.

rows.decision: Do not promote Monster Field Guide to implementation after the startup-only fixture pass.
rows.rationale: The exact disposable target is available and safe, but the fixture lacks synthetic users and therefore cannot yet prove per-player hidden-state projection or authority. Complete one native user-management setup and two-client read/permission test before any product build or readiness claim.

rows.decision: Promote World Doctor / Campaign Health to the newest conditional fresh-search candidate; keep Thin Client Player Relay open and Dungeon Master's Forge backburnered.
rows.rationale: World Doctor addresses a recurring GM/host costâ€”finding what will break in a complex world before an update or game nightâ€”and has a clearer paid trigger than generic player logistics. Foundry backup/migration, link repair, file cleanup, and document recovery tools occupy parts of the space, so diagnosis plus evidence-linked reversible repair must win a direct buyer trial.

rows.decision: Do not implement World Doctor until a synthetic-defect fixture and real GM price/pilot test pass.
rows.rationale: The category can collapse into a prettier backup, generic warning dashboard, or stale dedupe tool. Require snapshot/preview/repair/reread/rollback evidence, a no-write campaign boundary, and qualified GMs choosing a non-zero price over their current workaround.

rows.decision: Test World Doctor as a one-time GM/host utility with no subscription assumption.
rows.rationale: Upgrade breakage creates a credible GM pain signal, but Foundry backup/snapshot and hosting support cover recovery. Test only the narrower preflight diagnosis plus evidence-linked reversible repair at $15, $25, and $39 one-time anchors.

rows.decision: Reject World Doctor if backup, support, or generic compatibility warnings are good enough.
rows.rationale: The product must name the affected object, show evidence, preview a narrow repair, verify the authoritative result, and provide recovery. A warning list or duplicate finder leaves the hard diagnostic work with the GM and is not a defensible paid product.

rows.decision: Open Battle Director / Adaptive Encounter Audio as a fresh challenger; keep World Doctor conditional and Dungeon Master's Forge backburnered.
rows.rationale: Audio has a visible, repeated session payoff and category-level paid precedent, but Minstrel, Combat Music Master, Dynamic Soundscapes, Soundscape Adventure, and Playlist Plus cover meaningful pieces. The state-graph gap and buyer price remain unproven.

rows.decision: Do not implement Battle Director until a current-module comparison, Foundry hook fixture, and real one-time price/pilot trial pass.
rows.rationale: The candidate must be a no-touch encounter director rather than another playlist editor, must handle duplicate/repeated/unstoppable triggers safely, and must avoid bundled copyrighted audio.

rows.decision: Allow a bounded Foundry-first Battle Director prototype gate.
rows.rationale: Foundry v14 and D&D5e expose the needed signal/playback primitives, and local disposable code demonstrates GM-gated event/state handling. The prototype must remain synthetic, customer-audio-only, two-client, and fail closed on authority or synchronization errors.

rows.decision: Treat cross-VTT support as a neutral event graph plus separate adapters, not universal module parity.
rows.rationale: Roll20 and Owlbear have different extension/event surfaces, and D&D5e HP/condition semantics are system-specific. Preserve the portable recipe and asset mapping while keeping live adapters explicit.

rows.decision: Demote Battle Director; keep World Doctor conditional and Dungeon Master's Forge backburnered.
rows.rationale: Combat Music Master and Video Game Music close the core HP-trigger and adaptive-playback gap, while other current modules cover moods, intensity, region, scene, and cue workflows.

rows.decision: Do not implement Battle Director unless the direct competitor choice trial passes.
rows.rationale: Require 5/10 qualified GMs to prefer the state graph, 3/10 to choose a non-zero one-time price, 2/10 to schedule pilots, and a specific repeated unmet cost absent from the current module combination.

rows.decision: Open Scene Interaction Studio as the provisional fresh challenger; demote Quick Map Builder, Mobile Companion, and NPC Autopilot.
rows.rationale: The scene-interaction problem has a visible player payoff and explicit simplicity demand, while the alternatives are already occupied by current modules and apps. Raw capability is not enough; the UX and reliability gap remains unproven.

rows.decision: Do not implement Scene Interaction Studio until buyer choice and portability gates pass.
rows.rationale: The first slice must be a guided, testable recipe composer rather than a general visual scripting suite, and it must preserve a neutral recipe while keeping live VTT/system actions adapter-specific.

rows.decision: Demote Scene Interaction Studio and keep Dungeon Master's Forge backburnered; continue fresh search.
rows.rationale: Glyph materially covers the proposed visual program editor, event expansion, actions, system-aware rolls, and MATT import. No new product should clone that surface.

rows.decision: Exclude map, mobile, NPC-autopilot, audio, and visual-scene-automation clones from the next candidate shortlist.
rows.rationale: Each category now has a strong current implementation or several active competitors; a next candidate needs a distinct payer problem or direct buyer evidence.

rows.decision: Open Session Ready as the provisional fresh challenger; keep Dungeon Master's Forge backburnered and prior candidates demoted.
rows.rationale: Mixed-client session loss is a recurring GM/host cost with a visible green-light payoff. Existing modules cover point diagnostics and preload but do not, from their published descriptions, prove the combined readiness/fallback workflow.

rows.decision: Do not implement Session Ready until buyer choice, runtime observability, and fallback safety pass.
rows.rationale: The product must be a repeated session-control workflow, not a one-time diagnostic. It must fail open with a manual override, never report ready early, and avoid cloud dependency.

rows.decision: Demote Session Ready after direct capability audit; keep Dungeon Master's Forge backburnered and continue fresh search.
rows.rationale: Preload Tracker 2.2.0 implements the proposed readiness gate and recovery behavior, while Performance Optimizer and Axon cover profiles and diagnostics. A new bundle would not be a clean product gap.

rows.decision: Open Tactical Memory / Last-Seen Battlefield as the provisional fresh challenger.
rows.rationale: The candidate has a visible player payoff, direct recent community demand, a narrow source-scan gap, and a neutral portability contract. It may still be a tactical niche or free feature, so no implementation is authorized.

rows.decision: Do not implement Tactical Memory until buyer choice, privacy correctness, runtime, and price gates pass.
rows.rationale: The feature must be observer-scoped and historical, never omniscient; the trial must compare core fog, existing visibility tools, and manual markers and require a non-zero price plus pilot.

rows.decision: Keep Tactical Memory provisional but narrow the first slice to a live, temporary, observer-safe dungeon/combat overlay.
rows.rationale: Adjacent replay, movement, and visibility features do not exactly close the workflow, but the per-player observation and privacy problem is technically risky and the buyer segment may be narrow.

rows.decision: Keep Tactical Memory provisional with private player-local memory as the first safety slice; defer party sharing and portability.
rows.rationale: Paid visibility products show category spend and Foundry v14 exposes relevant observation hooks, but exact WTP and no-leak runtime behavior remain unproven.

rows.decision: Keep Tactical Memory as the provisional leader but do not select or implement it; retain the wide-market search.
rows.rationale: The direct gap and demo are cleaner than the alternatives, but buyer breadth and product-specific willingness to pay remain below the evidence required for a genuinely marketable product.

rows.decision: Demote Instant Encounter Board and retain Tactical Memory as the provisional leader only.
rows.rationale: The zero-prep pain is broad, but Dungeon Draw v14, Quickdraw, and SessionFlow cover most proposed capabilities. A new map product would be a clone without a buyer-named remaining failure.

rows.decision: Treat Tactical Memory rights risk as manageable and portability as a protocol-level hypothesis; keep the candidate provisional and unselected.
rows.rationale: The first slice can distribute only original functionality and local/procedural presentation, while Roll20 and Owlbear require independent adapter proofs. This resolves a shipping concern but does not meet the buyer or runtime gates.

rows.decision: Open TableSpeak as a fresh challenger without selecting it; keep Tactical Memory unselected.
rows.rationale: Live per-user table translation has a clearer recurring player benefit and cross-VTT direction than the current Tactical Memory candidate, but current evidence is community demand and adjacent tools, not buyer payment or runtime proof.

rows.decision: Cap the first TableSpeak slice at typed chat translation with optional captions; defer live voice.
rows.rationale: Voice translation magnifies cost, consent, attribution, latency, and trust risks, while Foundry exposes a chatMessage hook and a caption library surface. The narrow slice can be tested against external chat/voice workarounds.

rows.decision: Test TableSpeak as separate one-time BYOK/local and hosted usage-limited offers; do not subsidize translation usage.
rows.rationale: Provider APIs are metered and voice has separate plans. A narrow Foundry module can avoid cloud infrastructure, while a hosted service is a materially different business with recurring cost and privacy obligations.

rows.decision: Demote TableSpeak to a conditional challenger and reopen the wide fresh search.
rows.rationale: Discord and desktop translation products solve general multilingual communication. Only preservation of VTT semantics could justify a Foundry-specific product, and that has no buyer price or pilot proof.

rows.decision: Demote Guided Level-Up Concierge as a separate product.
rows.rationale: Current D&D5e and PF2e v14 packages already provide guided progression, validation, and tutorials. A generic replacement would be a duplicate or a crowded player-HUD suite.

rows.decision: Open Evidence Locker / Session Gallery as a conditional fresh challenger without selecting it.
rows.rationale: The recurring recall problem has a concrete player-visible payoff, but Foundry-native workflows and external products already cover broad handout sharing. Only automatic, permission-safe, VTT-semantic receipts justify further testing.

rows.decision: Reject generic handout delivery as the product; test only automatic Foundry-semantic receipts.
rows.rationale: LoreBox, TableWeaver, Roll20, Owlbear, and current Foundry packages make a general gallery or delivery tool easy to substitute. The narrow wedge must preserve links, permissions, revocation, and zero-extra-service setup.

rows.decision: Open World Clock Automator only as a fresh challenger for direct-package audit; do not implement it.
rows.rationale: The community request is concrete and the consequence demo is visible, but the buyer segment is narrower and current packages may already satisfy it.

rows.decision: Demote World Clock Automator as a standalone product; retain no-code consequence mechanics as reusable assets.
rows.rationale: Light Sources, About Time, Expedition Tracker, SessionFlow, Calendaria, and Glyph cover the broad behavior. Only a visual cross-system workflow that beats them on a repeated failure remains testable.

rows.decision: Keep Game Night Preflight / World Doctor as the leading conditional GM/host candidate without selecting it.
rows.rationale: Current pain is stronger and broader than the recent player-facing challengers, while current packages cover adjacent recovery and auditing. A narrow pre-update rehearsal is the remaining hypothesis.

rows.decision: Require a disposable-copy rehearsal, evidence-linked risk report, reversible repair, and $15/$25/$39/no-purchase test before World Doctor implementation.
rows.rationale: The candidate must beat Foundry backups plus support and current auditor/culprit workflows. A second-VTT diagnostic packet is a later portability gate; no live world may be mutated during proof.

rows.decision: Open Tactical Sketchbook / Collaborative Map Ink as the newest fresh conditional challenger; keep World Doctor conditional and Dungeon Master's Forge backburnered.
rows.rationale: A current high-engagement request contains explicit real-money language for better drawing and the demo is immediately understandable, while trade and mobile requests are already covered by current packages. Generic drawing is crowded, so only a fast scoped live-play workflow merits further testing.

rows.decision: Reject a generic Tactical Sketchbook editor, map generator, or drawing-settings bundle.
rows.rationale: Foundry core, Precise Drawing Tools, Advanced Drawing Tools, Dungeon Draw, Quickdraw, Roll20, and a premium early-access competitor occupy broad drawing improvements. The candidate must win on live speed, scoped layers, temporary cleanup, snapshots, and native export.

rows.decision: Require a Tactical Sketchbook $10/$20/$30/no-purchase test, three-session pilot, and Foundry permission fixture before implementation.
rows.rationale: Community demand and a premium competitor establish only directional category evidence. No purchase or portability claim is valid until qualified drawing-heavy GMs prefer the workflow over current modules and external tools and the fixture proves scope, reconnect, and no unintended source mutation.

rows.decision: Demote broad Tactical Sketchbook after current Gambit package correction; retain only temporary live-scene annotation as a narrow hypothesis.
rows.rationale: Gambit's Image Viewer already provides premium real-time media annotation and Gambit's Enhanced Drawing targets premium canvas drawing. Generic drawing is occupied and cannot be selected from community enthusiasm alone.

rows.decision: Open Adventure Navigator / GM Searchlight as the newest fresh conditional challenger; keep World Doctor conditional and Dungeon Master's Forge backburnered.
rows.rationale: A current v14 report describes a concrete session-time loss searching journals. The candidate has a visible time-saved demo, but generic search, campaign organization, and AI copilot tools cover adjacent jobs.

rows.decision: Reject a generic Adventure Navigator search bar, campaign wiki, AI copilot, or journal skin.
rows.rationale: Search and Highlight, Simple SearchBar, Quick Insert, Monk's Enhanced Journal, Campaign Codex, World & Campaign Builder, and Simulacrum already occupy those categories. The wedge must be deterministic active-scene context with exact source links and a short runbook.

rows.decision: Require an Adventure Navigator $15/$25/$39/no-purchase test, three-session pilot, and local content-index fixture before implementation.
rows.rationale: The product must beat free/paid search and organization tools for a real adventure-running GM incident, preserve permissions, avoid copying publisher content, reindex deterministically, and expose stale links.

rows.decision: Treat Adventure Navigator static API feasibility as permissioned read-only indexing only; do not infer runtime safety or legal clearance.
rows.rationale: Foundry v14 exposes JournalEntry links and permission methods, but stale IDs, hidden pages, ranking errors, publisher-content handling, and cross-VTT differences remain unverified.

rows.decision: Prioritize Adventure Navigator for the next buyer pilot; keep World Doctor as a separate second arm, Tactical Sketchbook dormant, and Dungeon Master's Forge backburnered.
rows.rationale: Adventure Navigator combines a recent concrete lookup incident with a safer read-only product boundary; this is prioritization for empirical testing, not product selection.

rows.decision: Do not call any candidate marketable until three non-zero price choices, two three-session pilots, and runtime/licensing/portability gates pass.
rows.rationale: A compelling demo or community request cannot substitute for buyer behavior, repeated use, safe implementation, and a credible portability boundary.

rows.decision: Open Rapid Encounter Board as a conditional challenger, not a selected product.
rows.rationale: The community pain is concrete and the demo is eye-catching, but current map-making, asset, and import tools are strong alternatives.

rows.decision: Reject a generic Rapid Encounter Board map editor, asset browser, or map-generator bundle.
rows.rationale: MapForge, FA Nexus, Moulinette, Scene Express, Mass Import, and external map makers already occupy those broad jobs. The candidate must win on temporary live staging, limited controls, scope safety, and native promotion.

rows.decision: Require Rapid Encounter Board $15/$25/$39/no-purchase testing, a three-session pilot, and one portable package boundary before implementation.
rows.rationale: A timed demo is not enough; the product must beat the buyer's current setup workflow without bundling copyrighted assets and must expose unsupported fields on Roll20 or Owlbear.

rows.decision: Keep Adventure Navigator first, World Doctor second, and Rapid Encounter Board as a third empirical arm; leave Tactical Sketchbook dormant and Dungeon Master's Forge backburnered.
rows.rationale: The new scene-staging signal is worth testing but is more directly competed than the two existing conditional candidates. No product is selected.

rows.decision: Do not market Rapid Encounter Board as a generic map studio, asset browser, or Dungeondraft replacement.
rows.rationale: MapForge already owns that commercial message and capability surface. The candidate must demonstrate a distinct live-session staging outcome with explicit scope and promotion behavior.

rows.decision: Require a MapForge head-to-head, $15/$25/$39/no-purchase choice, and three-session pilot before Rapid Encounter Board advances.
rows.rationale: MapForge's paid adoption is a useful category anchor, but it makes a direct buyer preference test more important, not less.

rows.decision: Keep Rapid Encounter Board third and conditional; competitor payment evidence does not select it.
rows.rationale: The strongest current payment signal belongs to the incumbent competitor, while the proposed narrow wedge has no product-specific WTP, runtime proof, or portable adapter evidence.

rows.decision: Open TableStart as a conditional fresh challenger, not a selected product.
rows.rationale: Player complexity and return-to-play friction are credible recruiting signals, but the broad category has strong free and premium substitutes and no product-specific WTP.

rows.decision: Reject generic player simplification, mobile sheets, hero selection, character creation, and ready checks as the TableStart product.
rows.rationale: Hide UI, Player Pilot, Claim Your Hero, Character Builder, Hero Mancer, AFK Ready Check, and SessionFlow already occupy those jobs.

rows.decision: Require a named onboarding or return-to-play incident, a comparator task, $10/$20/$30/no-purchase choice, and a three-session pilot before TableStart advances.
rows.rationale: A polished first-action demo can produce enthusiasm without solving a repeated table failure or earning payment.

rows.decision: Keep TableStart as a user-authored session-recipe layer with references, not a campaign workspace or bundled rules/tutorial library.
rows.rationale: This preserves a small implementation surface and lowers publisher-content risk while leaving VTT-specific adapters explicit.

rows.decision: Place TableStart fourth behind Adventure Navigator, World Doctor, and Rapid Encounter Board; no product is selected.
rows.rationale: The fresh player problem is attractive but less differentiated than the current empirical queue and still lacks buyer, runtime, and portability proof.

rows.decision: Open Tabletop Bridge as a conditional fresh challenger, not a selected product.
rows.rationale: In-person and hybrid GMs report multi-device coordination pain, but existing modules cover most individual components and no product-specific payment evidence exists.

rows.decision: Reject a Tabletop Bridge bundle that merely repackages common display, mobile, touch, or physical-dice features.
rows.rationale: Monk's Common Display, Physical Play Dice, TouchVTT, Player Pilot, Gaming Table, Ninjo's In-Person Tools, and Lock View already occupy those jobs.

rows.decision: Require a cold-start setup/recovery head-to-head, $20/$35/$50/no-purchase choice, and three-session real-table pilot before Tabletop Bridge advances.
rows.rationale: The value hypothesis is orchestration and reliability, so the comparison must measure configuration, secret safety, stale-client recovery, and switching profiles rather than feature count.

rows.decision: Keep Tabletop Bridge Foundry-first and hardware/provider-neutral; test only a neutral table-session record for portability.
rows.rationale: Hardware, display, player, and dice surfaces differ across VTTs, and an equivalent second-VTT mode is not statically established.

rows.decision: Place Tabletop Bridge fifth behind Adventure Navigator, World Doctor, Rapid Encounter Board, and TableStart; no product is selected.
rows.rationale: The workflow is eye-catching but narrower, component-crowded, and unproven on payer behavior, runtime, and second-VTT parity.

rows.decision: Reject a broad Tabletop Bridge feature bundle after the current-package audit.
rows.rationale: Ninjo's In-Person Tools, Digital Tabletops, Physical Play Dice, TouchVTT, Player Pilot, Gaming Table, and related modules cover the proposed display, touch, player, preload, and dice components.

rows.decision: Demote Tabletop Bridge from the active empirical queue to a negative control/parking lot.
rows.rationale: A current v14 competitor closes most of the feature gap, while no product-specific payment evidence supports a new module.

rows.decision: Revive Tabletop Bridge only after paid orchestration/recovery evidence appears.
rows.rationale: A buyer must name a failure the current package stack cannot solve and choose a non-zero price before implementation or recruitment.

rows.decision: Open VTT BridgeCheck as a conditional fresh challenger, not a selected product.
rows.rationale: Importer payment/adoption evidence is stronger than for the recent lanes, but the product must prove assurance value beyond source-specific importers and manual cleanup.

rows.decision: Reject a generic VTT importer, scraper, publisher-content copier, or cross-VTT parity promise.
rows.rationale: DDB-Importer, VTTA, R20Converter, PDF-to-Foundry, official packages, and Phils Map Migrator occupy broad import/scene-transfer jobs, while source terms and VTT semantics differ.

rows.decision: Require a named post-import failure, exact-importer head-to-head, $10/$25/$50/$75/no-purchase choice, and two real campaign pilots before BridgeCheck advances.
rows.rationale: Historical converter payment is category evidence; only buyer behavior for a receipt/repair assurance wedge selects the product.

rows.decision: Keep BridgeCheck local and user-owned at first; retain only a neutral receipt contract for portability.
rows.rationale: This lowers licensing and provider risk while preserving a path to separate source/target adapters after Foundry proof.

rows.decision: Place VTT BridgeCheck sixth behind Adventure Navigator, World Doctor, Rapid Encounter Board, and TableStart; keep Tabletop Bridge parked.
rows.rationale: BridgeCheck has a stronger payment signal but is episodic, source-adapter heavy, and still unproven on product-specific WTP, runtime, licensing, and portability.

rows.decision: Open LootFlow only as a fresh challenger for a buyer test, not as a selected product.
rows.rationale: Loot transactions are consumer-facing and visually demonstrable, but existing current packages already occupy the broad workflow.

rows.decision: Reject generic party inventory, shop UI, and loot-pile duplication.
rows.rationale: Item Piles, Quartermaster, Backpack, RPGX, The Stockpile, and hosted campaign tools cover the broad job; only a conflict-safe cross-VTT ledger remains hypothetical.

rows.decision: Demote LootFlow to a rejected seventh challenger/negative control and keep it out of implementation.
rows.rationale: No product-specific payment evidence is present, and the visual premium incumbent already demonstrates the strongest proposed features.

rows.decision: Revive LootFlow only after a named repeated transaction failure, non-zero price, and three-session pilot.
rows.rationale: A free shared chest or current Item Piles/Quartermaster flow may be sufficient; the buyer must reject those alternatives behaviorally.

rows.decision: Open TurnReady only as a fresh challenger for a buyer test, not as a selected product.
rows.rationale: The recurring combat pain is consumer-facing and demonstrable, but existing trackers, HUDs, and system advisors cover the broad surface.

rows.decision: Reject generic action tracking, HUD duplication, and cross-system rules inference.
rows.rationale: Action Keeper, Reaction Tracker, Stylish Action HUD, PF2e Combater, native tracker behavior, and system-specific tools already occupy these jobs.

rows.decision: Demote TurnReady to a rejected eighth challenger/negative control and keep it out of implementation.
rows.rationale: The payment signal belongs to category incumbents, while a new private turn card has no product-specific WTP or cross-system runtime proof.

rows.decision: Revive TurnReady only after a named accessibility/interruption failure, non-zero price, and three-session pilot.
rows.rationale: A current HUD or tracker may be good enough; the buyer must reject the exact alternative stack behaviorally before a fixture or adapter is built.

rows.decision: Run buyer validation in evidence order: VTT BridgeCheck, World Doctor, Adventure Navigator, Rapid Encounter Board, then TableStart.
rows.rationale: BridgeCheck has the strongest payment proxy and urgency; the remaining order balances recurring pain, competition, demo value, and technical risk without treating any candidate as selected.

rows.decision: Do not transfer price, payment, or pilot evidence from one candidate to another.
rows.rationale: A category incumbent or competitor subscription validates only category spending; each product must beat its exact current alternatives.

rows.decision: Keep all implementation paused until one candidate clears product-specific buyer, pilot, runtime, licensing, and portability gates.
rows.rationale: The scorecard resolves research order but leaves the go/no-go decision open.

rows.decision: Build the first BridgeCheck fixture as a Foundry-local, read-only disposable rehearsal.
rows.rationale: Foundry metadata and backups provide a plausible evidence boundary, while live mutation and external credential access are unsafe.

rows.decision: Reject DDB credentials, scraping, proxy impersonation, publisher-content retention, and live-world mutation.
rows.rationale: The importer's authentication and paid/proxy boundary belongs to the user/importer; BridgeCheck should inspect user-owned output and retain only receipt evidence.

rows.decision: Define portability as a versioned receipt contract, not a universal VTT converter.
rows.rationale: Roll20 transfer is primarily intra-platform and Owlbear metadata is compact; a shared record cannot prove equivalent campaign behavior.

rows.decision: Test a Roll20 user-mediated inventory and an Owlbear compact receipt adapter only after Foundry buyer/runtime proof.
rows.rationale: These adapters are technically bounded and rights-safer than account scraping, but neither should be built before the first product gate passes.

rows.decision: Keep BridgeCheck first in the buyer queue but narrow the go/no-go to Foundry post-import assurance.
rows.rationale: The technical audit supports a plausible local slice without proving product-specific WTP, exact-importer superiority, or cross-VTT parity.

rows.decision: Open Player Compass as a sixth conditional buyer-test candidate, not a selected product.
rows.rationale: Persistent player confusion has recurring session cost and a clear demo, but current HUD and accessibility modules cover much of the broad promise.

rows.decision: Reject a generic action HUD, combat tracker, sheet replacement, or rules engine for Player Compass.
rows.rationale: Token Action HUD, PF2e HUD, Argon, Stylish Action HUD, Foundry Navigator, and native sheets already cover those jobs.

rows.decision: Require a repeated player-control failure, exact HUD comparison, $10/$20/$30/$39/no-purchase choice, and three-session pilot before Player Compass advances.
rows.rationale: Category reach and a polished demo do not prove a GM will pay for automatic context selection.

rows.decision: Define Player Compass portability as a capability-manifest contract with separate system/VTT adapters.
rows.rationale: Action labels, availability, permissions, and context semantics differ across systems; shared UI cannot prove cross-VTT behavior.

rows.decision: Move Player Compass to the first empirical buyer gate and VTT BridgeCheck to the second.
rows.rationale: Player Compass has recurring use and current premium UX payment signals; BridgeCheck has stronger urgency and migration payment proxies but is episodic.

rows.decision: Require Player Compass to beat the exact HUD/orientation stack, not merely look better.
rows.rationale: Stylish Action HUD, Token Action HUD, PF2e HUD, Argon, Foundry Navigator, and native sheets already solve much of the broad problem.

rows.decision: Keep all candidates unselected until the first buyer gate records non-zero price, pilot, runtime, licensing, and portability evidence.
rows.rationale: A recurring payer proxy and polished competitor show category spend but do not prove a new product gap or WTP.

rows.decision: Treat Stylish Action HUD responses as incumbent behavioral payment evidence, not Player Compass WTP.
rows.rationale: Users explicitly praise and pay for the incumbent, but its exact offer already covers much of the broad surface.

rows.decision: Require Player Compass to support minimal, non-cinematic, one-time-use positioning in its buyer test.
rows.rationale: Some users reject visual overload, AI-linked payment, or subscriptions even when they value a focused HUD.

rows.decision: Keep Player Compass first in the empirical queue, but do not transfer incumbent conversion to the new product.
rows.rationale: The remaining hypothesis is zero-setup context clarity, which must earn its own preference, price, and pilot evidence.

rows.decision: Open Resolve Relay as a new conditional challenger below the current empirical queue.
rows.rationale: Target-resolution friction is concrete and visually demonstrable, but current free modules and system-specific conventions are strong substitutes.

rows.decision: Make Resolve Relay a permission-preserving GM handoff, not a player write bypass or general rules engine.
rows.rationale: Foundry permissions and PF2e hidden-defense concerns are deliberate safety boundaries; direct mutation would create security, correctness, and licensing risk.

rows.decision: Test Resolve Relay with combat-heavy GMs at one-time prices against the exact current stack.
rows.rationale: The payer is the GM/host and the category has free high-quality tools, so a product-specific price choice is mandatory.

rows.decision: Treat cross-VTT support as a later action-envelope adapter test, not an initial parity promise.
rows.rationale: VTT permissions and system damage semantics diverge even when the handoff message is structurally similar.

rows.decision: Demote Resolve Relay to a negative control and reusable protocol asset.
rows.rationale: The exact package check finds current free target-aware modules covering most of the proposed paid workflow; reopen only for a named unmet system or table failure.

rows.decision: Retain intent-envelope, stale-request, and idempotent-undo patterns without building Resolve Relay now.
rows.rationale: These patterns remain useful for future permission-safe coordination, but they do not justify a standalone product while substitutes are strong.

rows.decision: Open TableLink as the next fresh conditional challenger ahead of Resolve Relay.
rows.rationale: Connectivity failure has higher urgency, a clearer GM payer, a visible demo, a hosting payment anchor, and a broader transport boundary.

rows.decision: Require TableLink to beat the exact free tunnel path and paid-host path before implementation.
rows.rationale: A generic tunnel is already available; the proposed value is reliability, verification, reconnect, diagnostics, and safe fallback.

rows.decision: Use a Foundry-first local HTTP and WebSocket gateway with no cross-VTT parity claim.
rows.rationale: Transport can be neutral while provider, auth, system, and hosting semantics remain adapter-specific.

rows.decision: Require user-mediated provider credentials, short-lived invites, explicit bind approval, no payload inspection, and a kill switch.
rows.rationale: A local connectivity utility must not silently expose a port, capture credentials, inspect game payloads, or leave an unbounded background gateway.

rows.decision: Demote generic TableLink gateway management after the exact Foundry Tunnel Manager comparison.
rows.rationale: A current free utility already manages providers, start/stop, logs, URLs, live status, and tunnel expiry or death notifications.

rows.decision: Open JoinProof / Game Night Gatekeeper as the next conditional challenger.
rows.rationale: The remaining wedge is a verified pre-session result for the exact player invite, not another tunnel or hosting service.

rows.decision: Require direct comparison against Foundry Tunnel Manager, a phone or remote-player check, the exact free tunnel, and a managed host.
rows.rationale: The buyer may obtain the same confidence for free or prefer managed hosting at every price.

rows.decision: Require an independent external probe and reject same-network-only green status.
rows.rationale: NAT loopback can make a local check pass while real players fail, so the core claim needs an independent vantage or an explicit user-mediated remote check.

rows.decision: Use a neutral health receipt for later VTT adapters without promising session or auth parity.
rows.rationale: URL and protocol checks travel better than Foundry-specific gateway or login behavior; Foundry remains the first implementation target.

rows.decision: Demote JoinProof to a negative control after the external-verification comparison.
rows.rationale: Foundry provides a remote connectivity check and generic monitors or a player/phone test cover basic reachability; the remaining semantic wedge is unproven.

rows.decision: Retain false-green, stale-session, and minimal health-receipt patterns as reusable assets.
rows.rationale: These patterns can improve a future reliability product without justifying a standalone verifier today.

rows.decision: Do not build JoinProof without an independent-vantage fixture and a named surviving failure.
rows.rationale: Same-network checks can be falsely green and a probe service creates operating and privacy costs.

rows.decision: Continue the fresh search for a recurring payer problem after JoinProof demotion.
rows.rationale: The current networking category is crowded and episodic; a recurring campaign failure may produce stronger product use and buyer value.

rows.decision: Open Session Pulse / Campaign Commitment as an eighth conditional challenger.
rows.rationale: Recurring quorum and cancellation pain is ordinary and consequential, but the candidate must beat free scheduling and communication tools on the consequence-aware fallback workflow.

rows.decision: Position Session Pulse as quorum and fallback, not another calendar.
rows.rationale: Doodle, Discord Events, Warhorn, Foundry, Campaign Builder, and SessionFlow occupy scheduling, RSVP, planning, and live tracking.

rows.decision: Require ordinary recurring groups as the baseline and paid or organized-play GMs as a separate segment.
rows.rationale: The payer may be a GM or organizer while players benefit; conflating these segments would overstate WTP.

rows.decision: Use a neutral event and attendance contract for later VTT adapters without copying contacts by default.
rows.rationale: Attendance is portable, but notification platforms, identity, and consent boundaries differ.

rows.decision: Treat Doodle Professional payment as category evidence only, not Session Pulse WTP.
rows.rationale: Doodle sells coordination features, but ordinary D&D groups may use its free plan, Discord, or messages instead.

rows.decision: Make avoided prep loss and an explicit quorum/fallback decision the Session Pulse offer.
rows.rationale: A better scheduling poll is crowded; the remaining value is deciding what the GM should do before more prep is wasted.

rows.decision: Measure ordinary campaigns separately from paid GMs and organized-play coordinators.
rows.rationale: The payer, consequence of cancellation, and acceptable price may differ materially across segments.

rows.decision: Test Session Pulse buy-once pricing separately from recurring notification maintenance.
rows.rationale: A local utility can be sold once, while hosted reminders and integrations create continuing cost and may be rejected as a subscription.

rows.decision: Do not promote Session Pulse until a named prep-loss incident beats the exact free stack.
rows.rationale: Doodle, Discord, Warhorn, Foundry, and ad-hoc messages are mandatory controls; category payment is insufficient without repeated product-specific preference.

rows.decision: Treat recurring GM-prep reports as recruiting evidence, not proof of a new product.
rows.rationale: The pain is strong, but current premium and free prep suites occupy the broad workspace category.

rows.decision: Do not open a generic prep canvas, generic AI prep tool, or generic scheduling product from the fresh scan.
rows.rationale: The defensible future wedge would be safe reuse of discarded preparation after a player pivot, and that requires a named failure and rights-safe fixture.

rows.decision: Keep Player Compass first, BridgeCheck second, World Doctor third, and Session Pulse eighth in the empirical queue.
rows.rationale: The rerank weights recurring use, urgency, payer clarity, competition, and direct payment evidence without transferring category WTP.

rows.decision: Keep all candidates unselected until buyer price, pilot, runtime, licensing, and portability evidence is collected.
rows.rationale: Fresh community pain and polished incumbents are not sufficient evidence of product-specific marketability.

rows.decision: Keep Player Compass as the first empirical gate, but narrow the offer to zero-setup, read-only context clarity.
rows.rationale: Foundry Navigator, Token Action HUD D&D5e, and PF2e HUD close broad action access and accessibility; a generic HUD or sheet replacement is not a gap.

rows.decision: Require separate D&D5e and PF2e capability adapters with a neutral manifest.
rows.rationale: System-specific action semantics, permissions, and sheet controls cannot be safely replaced by a universal rules engine.

rows.decision: Preserve the native sheet and make all Player Compass actions user-invoked.
rows.rationale: The product must not perform hidden document writes, infer hidden rules state, or silently replace existing HUD and sheet workflows.

rows.decision: Ship user-owned data references and capability IDs, not copied rules, compendium text, publisher art, or competitor code.
rows.rationale: D&D5e and PF2e publish distinct software, content, art, and platform terms; exact package and asset audits remain required.

rows.decision: Delay a second VTT until Foundry proof and test only the neutral read-only manifest/intent boundary.
rows.rationale: A portable record is plausible, but system semantics, permissions, sheet controls, and accessibility behavior are not portable by default.

rows.decision: Require a keyboard, screen-reader, low-resolution, focus, reconnect, permission, and context-transition fixture before promoting Player Compass.
rows.rationale: Package descriptions establish a hypothesis but cannot certify accessibility or safe per-user behavior.

rows.decision: Open Campaign Anchor / Version Harbor as a fresh conditional challenger, not a selected product.
rows.rationale: Version fragmentation and upgrade anxiety are strong consumer-GM pain signals, but Foundry portable installs and managed hosting are serious substitutes.

rows.decision: Define Campaign Anchor as a campaign-specific environment lock, clone-before-upgrade rehearsal, known-good launch, and rollback receipt.
rows.rationale: Another version list, compatibility badge, backup browser, or generic launcher would not beat the exact alternatives.

rows.decision: Target self-hosting GMs with long-running or paid campaigns, premium content, multiple worlds, or an upgrade near-miss.
rows.rationale: One-shot GMs, managed-host users, and module creators are negative controls for this consumer product.

rows.decision: Test Campaign Anchor at $15/$30/$49 or no purchase against manual portable installs, the exact backup routine, The Forge, and Molten.
rows.rationale: Hosting and official portable-install payment proxies do not prove willingness to pay for a local utility.

rows.decision: Require clone-before-migrate, deterministic rollback, no live-world mutation, no package-binary bundling, no license bypass, and no cloud upload.
rows.rationale: The product operates around user-owned game data and licensed runtime packages, so safety and rights are part of the product promise.

rows.decision: Keep Campaign Anchor Foundry-only until buyer and runtime proof; test only a neutral environment receipt on a second VTT later.
rows.rationale: World formats, migrations, package manifests, launch models, and rollback semantics are not cross-VTT-compatible by default.

rows.decision: Demote Campaign Anchor from a likely second gate to a conditional comparison arm.
rows.rationale: Foundry core backups/snapshots, portable installs, managed hosting, and document recovery close the broad backup, pinning, and launcher promise.

rows.decision: Retain only a campaign-specific environment receipt that proves clone, rehearsal, known-good launch, and rollback.
rows.rationale: The product must answer a play-tonight decision or recovery that the exact Foundry controls do not answer; a version list or backup browser is rejected.

rows.decision: Reopen Campaign Anchor only for a named self-hosting GM failure surviving Foundry snapshots, portable installs, managed hosting, and World Doctor.
rows.rationale: Community upgrade anxiety is recruiting evidence, not product-specific willingness to pay.

rows.decision: Treat Campaign Anchor portability as a reusable environment-receipt protocol, not a cross-VTT launch promise.
rows.rationale: World formats, package manifests, migration behavior, and launch models are platform-specific.

rows.decision: Keep Between Sessions / Campaign Projects as a parked comparison arm, not a selected product.
rows.rationale: The official D&D5e Bastion category and multiple current downtime modules close the broad â€œadd projectsâ€ promise.

rows.decision: If reopened, test only player submission, GM batch approval, reconciliation, deadlines, and auditable receipts.
rows.rationale: Another downtime tracker, Bastion sheet, or progress bar would duplicate current tools.

rows.decision: Require a named weekly-campaign workflow failure and a $10/$20/$39/no-purchase choice before reopening.
rows.rationale: Official content demand and active free modules are category signals, not product-specific WTP.

rows.decision: Retain a neutral project-state contract but defer system-specific checks, currency, item automation, and second-VTT claims.
rows.rationale: The project state can travel; resolution semantics cannot be assumed portable.

rows.decision: Keep Table Pact / Campaign Fit as a conditional fresh challenger, not a selected product.
rows.rationale: The session-zero pain is visible, but current safety modules, forms, checklists, and direct conversation are strong substitutes and no product-specific WTP exists.

rows.decision: If reopened, test only private answers, aggregate conflicts, versioned acknowledgements, and re-checks.
rows.rationale: A compatibility score, raw sensitive-answer dashboard, or generic safety-card duplicate would create trust risk and weak differentiation.

rows.decision: Limit portability to consent-safe categories, pact version, acknowledgements, and aggregate unresolved flags.
rows.rationale: Private preferences and interpersonal judgments cannot be exported as if they were portable game state.

rows.decision: Reject Resource Steward / Ammunition and Supply Tension as a broad market candidate.
rows.rationale: Ordinary tables frequently opt out of mundane bookkeeping and current modules, macros, native quantities, or hand-waving cover most broad demand.

rows.decision: If Resource Steward is reopened, test only survival-focused or paid GMs with a neutral resource-event ledger.
rows.rationale: The reusable wedge is consume/recover/lose/threshold/provenance, not copied rules text or a generic counter dashboard.

rows.decision: Keep Resource Steward portability at event and policy boundaries.
rows.rationale: Resource events can travel, but encumbrance, recovery, firearms, and survival semantics need explicit system adapters.

rows.decision: Reject Character Integrity Ledger as a broad new product.
rows.rationale: Character Tracker and yugen-tracker already cover the core audit value; no product-specific WTP or unmet incident rate is established.

rows.decision: If Character Integrity Ledger is reopened, test only a named unexplained-incident wedge with role filtering and an explicit revert preview.
rows.rationale: A generic audit duplicate or public suspicion surface would add privacy risk without differentiation.

rows.decision: Keep integrity portability to redacted events, identifiers, timestamps, provenance, and acknowledgement state.
rows.rationale: Raw character data, private biography, and person-level suspicion are not portable game state.

rows.decision: Do not begin CL-11 until a controlled E2 runtime canary proves representative Notice, pickup, and observation behavior through the shared kernel. Author cleanup/reset behavior before triggering the canary.
rows.next_review: After CL-10C canary receipt
rows.rationale: CL-10 is the first old Lodge Scene wired into the new shared runtime; static verification alone does not prove live event execution and state mutation.
rows.topic: Runtime canary gate before expanding the installer pattern

rows.decision: Do not guess which N3 east/west main-line portal binds to T2. The lower branch portal is T3; T2 orientation remains unresolved until accepted global railway geography or explicit user direction resolves it.
rows.rationale: The approved N3 art establishes the three-portal topology but does not itself provide trustworthy campaign-geography orientation.

rows.decision: Do not delete or wholesale recreate the verified T1/T2/T3/F1/F2 RegionBehaviors. Reconcile them later with narrow read-only diagnostics and patch only proven incompatibilities.
rows.rationale: The 16 existing late-game behavior source hashes were captured before Region metadata normalization and independently verified afterward.

rows.decision: Every REDO abandons the previous image prompt and rewrites from current-map visible physical requirements only. Do not mention failures, forbidden neighboring content, destinations, story meaning, puzzle solutions, Region logic, or future rooms in image prompts.
rows.rationale: Repeated railway-map failures showed that contaminated prompt context can reproduce unwanted geometry.

rows.decision: Use the canonical Item registry, one persistent state ledger, one shared runtime kernel, declarative Region behaviorSpec metadata, and small ExecuteScript RegionBehavior dispatchers. Runtime identity uses stable IDs, not visible names or mutable document IDs.
rows.rationale: This architecture centralizes Notice, observation, pickup, socket, gate, transition, and state handling while protecting Region geometry and verified late-game behaviors.
rows.topic: Central Lodge Region behavior runtime architecture

rows.decision: A successful INSPECT PASS is the approval event for the exact render and moves durable state directly to APPROVED. A separate APPROVE command is optional and redundant.
rows.rationale: The user requested removal of the redundant approval wait-state so the map workflow can continue consistently and be automated without an unnecessary manual gate.

rows.decision: Open Player Pocket / VTT Companion as a conditional empirical challenger, not a selected product.
rows.rationale: Foundry mobile limitations and hybrid-table demand are visible, and current competitors prove a GM payment proxy, but the broad category is crowded.

rows.decision: Test only a permission-scoped portable player-action contract, not a full mobile VTT.
rows.rationale: A full mobile client duplicates active competitors and multiplies system, canvas, app-store, and version-drift cost.

rows.decision: Limit Player Pocket portability to normalized snapshots, permitted actions, results, resource deltas, notifications, and explicit unsupported state.

rows.decision: Key caches by content, world, scene role, client profile, and settings.

rows.decision: Never silently publish or substitute a derivative.
rows.rationale: Unsupported formats, fidelity loss, and failed storage need explicit user-visible states.

rows.decision: Use three pulsing-circle strikes per extraction attempt. Score each strike 5/4/3/2/1/0 by nested radial accuracy bands; use 1500/1350/1200 ms full pulse cycles; final ore yield is the rounded average of the three scores.

rows.rationale: This makes mining a fast skill-based interaction with graded near-misses while preserving a maximum five-unit jackpot and zero for a severe miss.

rows.decision: Keep timing animation/input client-side but keep result resolution GM-authoritative: the client sends exactly three bounded strike scores and the GM recomputes final yield before mutating shared state or inventory.
rows.rationale: This preserves the proven authority/depletion architecture while replacing only the gameplay resolver.

rows.decision: Add a bullseye Test Mining Minigame tool beside Fishing Ponds in Region Controls; launch the production timing UI in explicit no-write test mode.
rows.rationale: This gives the GM a fast tuning/test path while protecting live vein state and player inventory.

rows.decision: Use live score-zone tinting plus a post-strike label for every hit; make 5/5 PERFECT an oversized bright-green flash event.
rows.next_review: Tune saturation/flash duration after playtest.
rows.rationale: This makes the timing quality legible while preserving the fast reaction-game feel.

rows.decision: Make rendered ring diameter the scoring source of truth and lower the pulse floor to 20 px. Keep Perfect restricted to <=26 px even though the visible center bullseye is 38 px.
rows.next_review: Tune diameter bands only after live playtest.
rows.rationale: The prior ratio model could award or display a result that did not match what the player could physically see. Diameter-based scoring keeps visual and mechanical thresholds coupled while preserving a rare Perfect window.

rows.decision: Keep the current expansion pass focused on raw ore/deposit nodes and preserve alloys/refined metals plus non-ore special resources in a future-expansion backlog.
rows.next_review: Review after ore catalogue, value, and use design is locked.
rows.rationale: This keeps the immediate catalogue and value/use balance pass coherent while retaining the researched Realms metallurgy for later systems.

rows.decision: Use a single fixed unit price for each ore and let the existing timing minigame determine recovered quantity.
rows.next_review: Review after exact per-ore prices are chosen.
rows.rationale: Ore is fungible compared with fish size/value variation, and fixed unit prices keep the economy legible while rewarding mining skill through quantity.

rows.decision: Scale mining difficulty by pulse speed only, add all nine ores to testing, and combine Fishing/Mining setup into the existing Regionwright HUD shell.
rows.next_review: Review after live GM HUD and non-GM remote-test observation.
rows.rationale: One scoring geometry keeps player learning consistent; speed creates ore-specific challenge. One gathering HUD avoids duplicate floating panels and can integrate modules through public APIs.

rows.decision: Accelerate only Very Rare and higher ore pulse cycles while preserving the shared scoring geometry and lower-tier timing.
rows.next_review: Review after another tester pass.
rows.rationale: Live testing showed the top ore profiles remained too forgiving. Speed is the established difficulty control and avoids changing what each score means.

rows.decision: Starting at Gold, shrink every positive-scoring diameter band progressively by ore tier while keeping low-tier geometry unchanged.
rows.next_review: Review after live tester pass.
rows.rationale: High-value ore should require both reaction speed and precision; enlarging the miss zone prevents upper tiers from remaining forgiving even when pulses are fast.

rows.decision: Add a smooth deterministic 30% center-biased acceleration curve to every ore pulse while preserving cycle duration and score thresholds.
rows.next_review: Review after live tester pass across low and high tier ores.
rows.rationale: This makes Perfect harder without introducing randomness. Players who notice the ring accelerating near the center can learn to compensate and anticipate the strike.

rows.decision: Create regionwright-hunting-gathering with a small Puzzle-HUD-style GM interface and runtime adapters to Fishing and Mining; keep Hunting/Gathering disabled until implemented.
rows.next_review: Review after the v0.1.0 scaffold and first Hunting design pass.
rows.rationale: This creates the final product boundary without prematurely merging proven subsystem logic or copying Studio complexity.

rows.decision: Require a dedicated module-owned Hunting Bow using an exact Regionwright flag, with no generic bow or name fallback.
rows.next_review: Review only if explicit hunting equipment variants are added later.
rows.rationale: There are too many bow variants to infer hunting compatibility safely, and a dedicated item keeps the minigame equipment contract clear.

rows.decision: Flatten Regionwright dialogs onto a translucent charcoal Foundry-like application surface and remove decorative card-style section containers.
